drhp.business: Sunrakshakk manufactures FMCG products (bath soap, toothpaste, detergent powder, toilet cleaner, liquid detergent, cosmetics), FMCG intermediates (soap noodles, specialty chemicals), edibles (savouries, spices), and processed textile fabrics (100% cotton, RFD, bleached, dyed, printed and yarn-dyed fabrics). It serves a base of over 200 companies on a pan-India basis, including as a manufacturing partner to large FMCG brands that outsource production, alongside its own textile-processing operations.
drhp.expansion: The Guwahati facility (soap-noodle and cosmetics capacity) was commissioned and ramped up progressively from January 2026, running at approximately 45-55% capacity utilisation across both lines as of the Q4 FY26 earnings call, with management indicating it is well positioned to serve Assam, the broader Northeast, Bengal and Bihar markets. The Bhilwara edibles facility (savouries and spices) became fully operational and has been contributing to revenue since September 2025. risks.note: The Company relies on imported and crude-oil-linked inputs (palm oil, LAB/LABSA and packaging materials); the Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption sharply raised LABSA, soda ash and packaging costs, a key watch-item for FMCG and FMCG-intermediates profitability.

Fair value of future cash flows may fluctuate from changes in market prices, comprising interest rate risk, currency risk and price risk, affecting investments, receivables, deposits and financial liabilities.
Changes in market interest rates affect interest income and expense; the Company holds a mix of fixed and variable-rate instruments including cash credit and term loans from banks.
The Company undertakes transactions in foreign currencies; exchange-rate volatility affects revenue from export markets and the cost of imports, primarily raw materials.
The Company is exposed to fluctuations in the price of key raw materials and finished goods, and to changes in product demand, in both domestic and international markets.
The Company is exposed to counterparty default risk mainly from operating activities (trade receivables) and financing activities including bank deposits.

Risk of financial distress or unusually high financing costs from a shortage of liquid funds if business conditions unexpectedly deteriorate, given the Company's need for both short-term operational and long-term capex funding.

A longer or broader Middle East conflict, renewed trade tensions or elevated global energy prices could weaken growth and raise input costs, given the Company's reliance on crude-oil-linked raw materials.
